Marathon Petroleum fell 1.04% today to $389.44, extending a two-week slide. The decline comes despite oil prices remaining elevated—U.S. crude at $96.41 per barrel and global oil at $114.89—suggesting the market is pricing in relief from Middle East tensions as diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran gain traction. When geopolitical risk recedes, refiners like Marathon typically sell off because the crisis premium on oil prices evaporates, even though the company benefits from higher crude costs in normal times.

The broader headwind is policy uncertainty around a potential diesel export ban, which analysts warn could disrupt refiner margins and global supply chains. With refineries running at 94% capacity and diesel inventories relatively tight at 107 million barrels, any export restriction would constrain what refiners can sell abroad and potentially lower domestic fuel prices—squeezing profitability even as crude inputs remain costly.
